hints: For $f(x) = 2 - 3\cos x$, evaluate minimum $2 - 3(1) = -1$ and maximum $2 - 3(-1) = 5$.
walkthrough:
Determine the range of $f(x) = 2 - 3\cos x$ on $0 \le x \le 2\pi$ (where $-1 \le \cos x \le 1$):
$$\text{Minimum value} = 2 - 3(1) = -1$$
$$\text{Maximum value} = 2 - 3(-1) = 5$$
$$\text{Range of } f: \quad -1 \le f(x) \le 5 \quad (\text{or } [-1, 5])$$

hints: Sketch one full cycle of $y = 2 - 3\cos x$ starting at $(0, -1)$, rising through $(\pi/2, 2)$ to $(\pi, 5)$, and returning to $(2\pi, -1)$.
walkthrough:
Sketch the cosine wave $y = 2 - 3\cos x$ over $[0, 2\pi]$:
- Starts at minimum turning point $(0, -1)$.
- Crosses midline $y = 2$ at $\left(\frac{\pi}{2}, 2\right)$.
- Reaches maximum turning point at $(\pi, 5)$.
- Crosses midline at $\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}, 2\right)$.
- Finishes at minimum turning point $(2\pi, -1)$.

hints: Identify the largest interval $[0, p]$ where $g(x) = 2 - 3\cos x$ is strictly increasing (from $x = 0$ to $x = \pi$).
walkthrough:
For $g(x)$ to possess an inverse, it must be a strictly monotonic one-to-one function.
Starting at $x = 0$, $g(x) = 2 - 3\cos x$ increases strictly until its maximum at $x = \pi$.
$$\text{Largest value of } p = \pi$$

hints: Set $y = 2 - 3\cos x \implies 3\cos x = 2 - y \implies \cos x = \frac{2 - y}{3}$.
walkthrough:
Set $y = 2 - 3\cos x$ and isolate $\cos x$:
$$3\cos x = 2 - y \implies \cos x = \frac{2 - y}{3}$$

Take the inverse cosine:
$$x = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2 - y}{3}\right)$$
$$g^{-1}(x) = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2 - x}{3}\right)$$
